verdict.headline: Pangram catches most first-draft AI text but nearly 4 in 10 attacks slip through after a rewrite, so it should not be anyone's only check.
findings: Caught on first try: 283/350 = 80.9% (95% CI 76.4-84.6%), but evaded after rewrites: 139/350 = 39.7% (95% CI 34.7-44.9%) -- a single rewrite pass roughly doubles the escape rate.

Forger Hermes-3 8B was evaded only 3/90 = 3.3% (95% CI 1.1-9.3%) and GLM 5.3 Flash evaded 68/80 = 85.0% (95% CI 75.6-91.2%) -- these two do not overlap, so GLM 5.3 Flash reliably evades far more than Hermes-3 8B.

Kimi K3.1 Pro (evaded 52/90 = 57.8%, 95% CI 47.5-67.5%) and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 (evaded 16/90 = 17.8%, 95% CI 11.2-26.9%) have non-overlapping CIs too, so DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017's text was caught much more reliably.

Genuine human paragraphs wrongly flagged: 3/58 = 5.2% (95% CI 1.8-14.1%), and the Science paper's false-alarm rate (3/27 = 11.1%, 95% CI 3.9-28.1%) overlaps the Court opinion and Government report rates (0/18 and 0/13), so no real difference between documents is established.
advice: Treat a 'clean' Pangram score as weak evidence, not proof -- a motivated person who revises a flagged draft has roughly a 39.7% chance of getting past it.
Expect occasional false alarms on genuine human writing (3/58 = 5.2% in this test) and always allow the accused person to explain or show drafts/history before acting on a flag.
Never use the detector as the sole basis for a grade, hire, or publication decision -- pair it with a human review of context, sourcing, and the writer's own process.

patterns.pattern: Heavier use of hard numbers and citations
patterns.explanation: Evading text leans on concrete figures, statutes, and case cites almost twice as often as caught text, which reads as more generic/abstract.
patterns.evidence: digits_per_100w 4.8 (evaded) vs 2.5 (caught); citations_per_100w 1.3 vs 0.5 (e.g. 'Conn. App. 640, 646, 700 A.2d 1151 (1997)')

patterns.explanation: Detector-evading forgeries say less; caught forgeries run noticeably longer, giving the detector more text to find AI patterns in.

patterns.pattern: Punchier, more variable sentence rhythm vs uniform length
patterns.explanation: Evading text mixes short and long sentences (higher variance, lower average length); caught text sentences run longer and more uniform, closer to typical AI cadence.

patterns.pattern: Flourish-y verbs and self-narration flag as AI
patterns.explanation: Caught examples repeatedly use ornate phrasing and 'we did X' framing ('we delved into', 'honed in on', 'unveiled') that reads as stylistically inflated; evaders stick closer to flat, matter-of-fact reporting language. This is suggestive from the quotes, not confirmed by a clean numeric split since first_person_per_100w differs only slightly (0.4 vs 0.7).
patterns.evidence: quote: 'we delved into the affiliations' / 'honed in on three significant funders'

analysis.summary: Forgeries that fooled the detector were shorter, blunter, and packed with concrete numbers and legal/report citations, while caught forgeries were longer and used more flowery, narrator-ish language. The successful ones also went through editing that trimmed sentence length even further after the first draft.

facts:
Valid attacks: 350 (attempted 360, errors 10, rejected 0)
Caught on first try: 283/350 = 80.9% (95% CI 76.4–84.6%)
Evaded after rewrites: 139/350 = 39.7% (95% CI 34.7–44.9%)
Genuine human paragraphs wrongly flagged: 3/58 = 5.2% (95% CI 1.8–14.1%)
Forger GLM 5.3 Flash: evaded 68/80 = 85.0% (95% CI 75.6–91.2%); caught first 36/80 = 45.0% (95% CI 34.6–55.9%); avg AI score first 46% -> best 20%
Forger Kimi K3.1 Pro: evaded 52/90 = 57.8% (95% CI 47.5–67.5%); caught first 74/90 = 82.2% (95% CI 73.1–88.8%); avg AI score first 81% -> best 43%
Forger DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017: evaded 16/90 = 17.8% (95% CI 11.2–26.9%); caught first 84/90 = 93.3% (95% CI 86.2–96.9%); avg AI score first 91% -> best 77%
Forger Hermes-3 8B (own Modal GPU): evaded 3/90 = 3.3% (95% CI 1.1–9.3%); caught first 89/90 = 98.9% (95% CI 94.0–99.8%); avg AI score first 98% -> best 92%
Document Science paper: evaded 29/114 = 25.4% (95% CI 18.3–34.1%); false alarms 3/27 = 11.1% (95% CI 3.9–28.1%)
Document Court opinion: evaded 51/116 = 44.0% (95% CI 35.3–53.0%); false alarms 0/18 = 0.0% (95% CI 0.0–17.6%)
Document Government report: evaded 59/120 = 49.2% (95% CI 40.4–58.0%); false alarms 0/13 = 0.0% (95% CI 0.0–22.8%)
